title: P-036: Duplicate event should not create new RI or display again
summary: passive_ri_ingest runs on two consecutive days. On day 2, the same email-sourced signal for Jeff Wayman is re-detected (same sender, same thread, same event_at date). ri_events.append() should detect the duplicate via the dedupe hash and return was_appended=false. passive_ri_ingest should place the event in duplicates_skipped with ri_assessment.status=duplicate and display_recommendation=suppress. The brief should NOT surface a second proposal for the same touch.

steps.label: Day 1: First ingest — event written
steps.description: passive_ri_ingest.py processes an email signal from jeff@example.com on 2026-05-23. Event is new; ri_events.append returns was_appended=true. Result: events_written=1, ri_assessment.status=proposed.

steps.label: Day 2: Same signal re-detected
steps.description: The email from jeff@example.com on 2026-05-23 is still in the inbox JSON (not removed after processing). passive_ri_ingest runs again. Same source_id/hash, same event_at, same entities. ri_events.append returns was_appended=false (duplicate).

steps.label: Brief does not re-surface the duplicate
steps.description: Day 2 brief proof row shows ri_assessed_duplicate:1. Brief does NOT say 'I propose a touch for Jeff Wayman' for the duplicate. No RI language about Jeff Wayman unless there is a NEW signal on day 2.

acceptance_criteria: ri_events.append returns was_appended=false for exact duplicate
brief proof row shows ri_assessed_duplicate; no RI language re-surfaced
anti_patterns: writing a second proposed event for the same signal
claiming 'I found a new relationship signal for Jeff Wayman' on day 2
no dedupe check — events_written count increases every daily run for static inbox data
